request.args: Write a Python example that splits a string at one index into a first piece and a second piece. Use these sizes and values: data = 'abcdefghij', n = len(data), cut = int(n*0.9), train = data[:int(n*0.9)], val = data[int(n*0.9):]. Standard library and numpy only; nothing imported from the source. One comment per step, in the words the reader already knows: string, characters, index, slice, train piece, held-back piece. Steps: set the string and its length; slice the first piece up to the index; slice the second piece from the same index; print both pieces; print that train + val equals data and that the lengths add up to n, so no character is shared or missing. Do not print or state any output.

block.title: Splitting a string at one index
block.brief: One index cuts a string into a train piece and a held-back piece that together rebuild the original.
block.code:
# the string of characters we want to split, and how many characters it has
data = 'abcdefghij'
n = len(data)

# the index where we cut: 90% of the way along the string
cut = int(n * 0.9)

# the train piece: slice from the start up to (not including) the index
train = data[:int(n * 0.9)]

# the held-back piece: slice from that same index to the end
val = data[int(n * 0.9):]

# look at the two pieces
print('train piece:', train)
print('held-back piece:', val)

# the pieces joined back together are the original string
print('train + val == data:', train + val == data)

# their lengths add up to n, so no character is shared or missing
print('len(train) + len(val) == n:', len(train) + len(val) == n)
print('cut index:', cut, '| sizes:', len(train), len(val))
